rows.question: For about how long were the heaters of the tank that later exploded on Apollo 13 run on ground power before launch, and what did the investigating board say started the explosion?
rows.answer:
Before launch, the tank's heaters were run on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours, which emptied the tank [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)".

The Apollo 13 Review Board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)".

The opened notes do not state that the board named the thermostatic switches as the cause, so I have left that out.

rows.question: The astronaut who caught German measles before Apollo 13 set off a crew swap. What office did the astronaut brought in by that swap later win, and what happened?
rows.answer:
The astronaut was Charlie Duke, whose German measles started the swap. The astronaut brought in was Jack Swigert, who became Apollo 13 command module pilot in place of Ken Mattingly. Swigert later won a seat in the US House of Representatives: [[jack-swigert]] "[stated] Was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1982 but died before taking office (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)". The notes do not say which district he won, and they do not give the cause or date of his death.

Supporting facts: [[charlie-duke]] "[stated] Caught German measles from a friend's 3-year-old son about three weeks before the Apollo 13 launch (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"; [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Backup lunar module pilot Charlie Duke caught German measles and exposed the crews (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"; [[jack-swigert]] "[stated] Apollo 13 role is prime command module pilot (was backup command module pilot, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)".

During the landing, Collins stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia: [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)".

The notes do not say more about what he did during the landing.

rows.question: What was the improvised "mailbox" on Apollo 13 made from, and how did the crew build it?
rows.answer:
The "mailbox" was an improvised CO2 scrubber adapter, made from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] Engineers devised an adapter from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The crew built it from radioed instructions. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The crew built it from radioed instructions (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

It was needed because the command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square and the lunar module's were round. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square and the lunar module's were round (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

Mission Control Houston's engineers devised the adapter. [[mission-control-houston]] "[stated] Engineers there devised the Apollo 13 carbon dioxide scrubber adapter (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The notes do not give the specific build steps or dimensions.

rows.question: How did the Cortright report describe the switch failure?

It also recommended removing all electrical equipment from inside the oxygen tank pressure vessel. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Recommended removing all electrical equipment from inside the oxygen tank pressure vessel (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)"

The notes do not say in detail how the report described the switches themselves. The fire is traced to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2. rows.question: Put every 1970 date the brain records for Apollo 13 in order, with what happened on each.
rows.answer:
Here are the 1970 dates the brain records for Apollo 13, in order. Each quote is copied exactly from an opened note, including its `[stated]` tag.

1. **1970-04-06:** Blood tests from the physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Blood tests from the 1970-04-06 physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

2. **1970-04-10:** The crew swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference, so Jack Swigert replaced Ken Mattingly as command module pilot. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10 (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)" [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Command module pilot is Jack Swigert (was Ken Mattingly, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

3. **1970-04-11:** Apollo 13 launched. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Launched 1970-04-11 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

4. **1970-04-13:** Oxygen tank No. 2 exploded about 56 hours into the flight. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)" The mission goal also changed from a lunar landing at Fra Mauro to a safe return to Earth, by a Mission Control abort decision. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Mission goal became a safe return to Earth (was a lunar landing at Fra Mauro, changed 1970-04-13 by Mission Control abort decision) (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

5. **1970-04-17:** The crew, using the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat, splashed down. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down on 1970-04-17 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

6. **June 1970:** The Cortright board report on the explosion was published. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Published in June 1970 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)" The board traced the explosion to tank No. 2's thermostatic switches. [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"
